# VIZ browser SDK and HF15 agent permissions

## Vendored artifact provenance

- Upstream: [VIZ-Blockchain/viz-js-lib](https://github.com/VIZ-Blockchain/viz-js-lib/tree/8a60784aa86a5dda30e49a6f339277ce3a67d28f), commit `8a60784aa86a5dda30e49a6f339277ce3a67d28f` (package version `0.18.2`). This repository is the authoritative viz-js-lib / browser `viz.min.js` source; no extension is bundled.
- `viz.min.js` SHA-256: `8e723c5d8b81b77d7d003f78b07c292e064ea7a56af9ff58186aa97e472362e3`. The vendored bytes equal the local upstream browser build, not the older npm release whose gitHead is `d6f5cc4869d15e68205b968f9bc991a8d0be2ff2`.
- License: [MIT](https://github.com/VIZ-Blockchain/viz-js-lib/blob/8a60784aa86a5dda30e49a6f339277ce3a67d28f/LICENSE); the upstream copyright/license notice is included in the adjacent `LICENSE` file.
- Built outside the application repository using Node `22.22.0`, npm install with `--legacy-peer-deps --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund`, then `npm run build-browser`. Upstream webpack `1.15.0` does not honor its `node.async_hooks: 'empty'` setting with Bluebird `3.7.2`: the build config alone was adjusted to append `new webpack.IgnorePlugin(/^async_hooks$/)` to `makePlugins(options)`. No upstream runtime/serializer source was patched. The final build has no compilation errors.
- Dependency-resolution snapshot SHA-256 (`package-lock.json` in the isolated build): `36f9a1789253e0302a34495da9f2e219aadbdda995cf27ddd3a9a651d024560b`. This is provenance evidence, not a promise that future semver-based installs reproduce those bytes. Upstream uses legacy build dependencies; app dependency files are unchanged.

## Protocol source

Verified against [viz-cpp-node commit `ac7b98d1c5e4f747f79035b2cbd533a3eaa06699`](https://github.com/VIZ-Blockchain/viz-cpp-node/tree/ac7b98d1c5e4f747f79035b2cbd533a3eaa06699):

- [`agent_operations.hpp`](https://github.com/VIZ-Blockchain/viz-cpp-node/blob/ac7b98d1c5e4f747f79035b2cbd533a3eaa06699/libraries/protocol/include/graphene/protocol/agent_operations.hpp), `agent_operations.cpp`, `agent_evaluator.cpp` and `operations.hpp` are the consensus evidence.
- [Agent access](https://github.com/VIZ-Blockchain/viz-cpp-node/blob/ac7b98d1c5e4f747f79035b2cbd533a3eaa06699/docs/protocol/operations/agent-access.md) and [database API](https://github.com/VIZ-Blockchain/viz-cpp-node/blob/ac7b98d1c5e4f747f79035b2cbd533a3eaa06699/docs/plugins/database-api.md#get_agent_permissionsaccount) explain the UI/RPC semantics.
- `set_agent_permission`, static-variant operation ID **105**, requires the principal's **active** authority. Exact order: `account`, `agent_name`, `agent_key`, `operations` (`flat_set<string>`), `expiration` (`time_point_sec`), `addons` (`flat_set<string>`), `extensions` (`[]`). The SDK wrapper is `setAgentPermission`; RPC is `database_api.get_agent_permissions(account)` / `getAgentPermissionsAsync(account)`.
- Epoch `1970-01-01T00:00:00` means unlimited. Both lists empty revoke the named agent; null public key is valid for revoke. A past expiration also revokes on chain, but the grant UI rejects past dates to avoid accidental revocation. Reissuing a name replaces its key, scopes and expiration. Addon-only grants are valid and grant no on-chain permissions.
- At most 16 agents per principal. A key cannot belong to two names on the same principal. Addons are opaque off-chain scopes: at most 10, each 1–63 UTF-8 bytes, with no comma in a value. The UI splits comma-separated values, deduplicates them and rejects private-key-shaped values before any public preview.
- Never delegable: `set_agent_permission`, `proposal_update`, `account_update`, `recover_account`, `change_recovery_account`, `set_account_price`, `set_subaccount_price`, `target_account_sale`. Virtual operations (including `cancel_paid_subscription`, which inherits `virtual_operation` in `chain_virtual_operations.hpp:237`), unknown names, deprecated aliases and wildcards are excluded. The protocol recognises 59 canonical delegable names (67 broadcastable minus 8 forbidden); the selectable/build allowlist excludes the retired `vote`, `content` and `delete_content`, leaving 56 current scopes. Historical RPC rows using those names remain readable/revocable, but the removed operations cannot be selected or reissued. The protocol set is verified independently from `operations.hpp`, both virtual-operation headers and `agent_operations.cpp`. It does not widen grants when new operations appear. Agents cannot satisfy master/other/nested account authority; proposal create/delete do not confer approvals.
- All permissions disappear on master/active field inclusion in account update (even unchanged authority), recovery or account sale. Regular-only changes preserve agents.

## User-facing behavior and safety

VIZ **Manage → Ключи агента / Agent keys** uses the shared accessible dialog with a labelled native multi-select for operations. Multiple selections are captured exactly; Edit preselects current saved scopes. Load permission rows; Edit fills every current public field; Revoke fills an explicit revoke action that still needs Preview/Send and final confirmation. Other chains have no agent UI or support added.

Generate uses `crypto.getRandomValues` locally. The private WIF is masked in an unnamed, nonserialized handoff field. Save it to a password manager and hand it only to the intended agent over a secure channel. Explicit acknowledgement covers that exact generated key. There is no clipboard API, download, local/session storage or logging of this key. Close, route change and vault lock clear the field/references; an unsaved generated public key is also discarded. JavaScript garbage collection cannot guarantee physical memory erasure. The visible form is the intended handoff surface; do not reveal it while screen sharing.

All operation scopes, public key, expiration and addons appear in the confirmation summary. One form owns grant/update/revoke single-flight submission. Route/account/lifecycle and vault guards are checked before preparation, after connection/authority lookup, and **after the final asynchronous preparation immediately before signing/broadcast**. For limited grant/update, after SDK TAPOS preparation the broadcaster fetches fresh `get_dynamic_global_properties.time`, validates canonical UTC times against both the chain head and current local clock, then sets transaction expiration to `min(SDK transaction expiration, permission deadline minus one second)`. If no future safe window remains, or chain/transaction time is malformed/unavailable, it fails before signing. The permission expiration is never extended or rewritten; unlimited and explicit revoke keep SDK transaction validity unchanged. This strictly earlier transaction bound prevents a delayed grant from being included after its permission expires and thereby becoming an evaluator revoke (`agent_evaluator.cpp:99–114`).

Grant/update/revoke sends one synchronous-broadcast attempt, with no automatic retry. Success requires an inclusion receipt with a 40-hex transaction `id`, positive int32 `block_num`, nonnegative int32 `trx_num`, and boolean `expired:false` (`network_broadcast_api.cpp:205`). `expired:true` or `trx_num:-1` is failure, not success (`:225`); empty/malformed receipts and transport errors are unknown, not confirmation. Failed/unknown sends show an error and retain the generated handoff and saved-key acknowledgement while the dialog remains current; only confirmed inclusion clears it. Check public permissions before manually submitting again. Active-key verification uses the existing common broadcaster; agent keys are not imported as account login credentials.

## Regression checks (no live writes)

```sh
node tests/v3-viz-agents.js
DPOS_QA_STANDALONE=1 python3 tests/browser/viz-agents.py
node tools/web-checks.cjs
git diff --check
```

The Node test compares the complete unsigned transaction bytes to an independent encoder, including ID105, every field, epoch and both extension sets; it exercises the real SDK positional wrapper and offline signatures. Its independent protocol fixture checks exactly all 56 current selectable scopes, rejects the 3 retired names and still reads historical protocol rows, virtual-scope rejection without substitutes, inclusion/expired/malformed/transport receipt classification and one-attempt behavior. The broadcaster accepts the real SDK's Date-valued TAPOS transaction expiration separately from strict canonical protocol strings; invalid Dates fail closed. Node integration regressions use the actual vendored `_prepareTransaction()` with only read-only RPC mocked and cover both bounds. Browser TAPOS also delegates to that real SDK method, preserving real preparation and signing. Counter-signer branch tests prove elapsed deadlines, malformed/unavailable clocks and unsafe validity windows stop with zero signatures/broadcasts; limited validity is bounded while unlimited/revoke stay unchanged. The connected-CDP browser test uses fresh synthetic vault accounts, intercepted RPC/broadcaster and **9 actually signed intercepted attempts** (4 included receipts and 5 failed/unknown outcomes). It proves failed/unknown handoff retention/no retry, elapsed confirmation/authority/TAPOS deadlines and chain-ahead-local rejection with zero signatures, and an actual signed near-deadline grant bounded one second before permission expiration. It also covers timezone-sensitive expiry, confirmation cancellation, generated-key handoff/redaction, grants/revokes/addon-only grants, stale route/account during TAPOS, duplicate submit, delayed reads, RU/EN errors and focus trapping/restoration. Standalone mode launches an isolated Chromium and connects over CDP without copying any signed-in profile. Default mode uses the existing relay; some Playwright/Chromium combinations reject preexisting service-worker targets during attachment, in which case standalone mode is the supported fallback.

Read-only live check: `https://api.viz.world`, `get_agent_permissions("on1x")` returned `[]`; `get_hardfork_version()` returned `"4.1.0"`. No grant, revoke, transaction or other mainnet write was broadcast. An empty live result validates availability, not a real nonempty permission row; populated-row behavior is verified by the protocol-backed browser fixture.
